content:
Requirement R19 (input): Initiate Handover Request. Fixed modalities: Touch and Keyboard. Intent: Allow the pilot to request a control handover of a UAV..

We will design this requirement in three sequential layers, all within THIS conversation: Function first, then Behaviour, then Structure. Conduct the sequence yourself — when a layer is agreed, state its final label clearly and move to the next.
- Functions: propose 2-3 genuinely distinct candidates labeled F-19.1, F-19.2, ... Distinct means each opens a different interaction goal — not the same goal reworded.
- Behaviours: one distinct interaction idea per fixed modality pathway (e.g. one Touch-only, one Keyboard-only), plus a Mixed pathway if it adds real value beyond the two. Labeled Be-19.<F>.1, Be-19.<F>.2, ... using the closed F index.
- Structures: 2-3 distinct sets of concrete HMI elements, labeled S-19.<F>.<Be>.1, ... using the closed F and Be indices.

Start with the Function candidates now (state the intent back first). The designer closes the whole requirement at the end.

**Intent restated:** R19 lets the pilot dispatch a request to hand a UAV's control back to the UAV Pilot — the request/negotiation step (8.1), not the actual link-break commit (that's R20 territory).

This is the structural mirror of R09 (takeover request). Function candidates:

**F-19.1 — Dispatch handover request for a selected UAV.**
The pilot's goal: signal intent to relinquish control of the currently-managed UAV, initiating the handover negotiation. Directly maps 8.1.1. This is the primary teleology.

**F-19.2 — Make the pilot aware of the UAV Pilot's response to the request.**
The goal: close the loop — pilot learns whether the handover was acknowledged/accepted (8.1.7). Distinct goal (awareness of a returned decision), not the dispatch itself.

**F-19.3 — Enable selection of which UAV to hand over (when multiple are managed).**
The goal: scope the handover to a specific UAV before requesting. Distinct from dispatch — it's target-scoping.

**My recommendation:** F-19.1 is the core of R19. F-19.2 is real but is almost certainly already covered by R08's notification stack (response arrives as a pilot notification) — flag: **Be/Structure for F-19.2 would be shared with R08/R10, not exclusive here.** F-19.3 mirrors the UAV-selection already established in R09/R12 and is arguably a precondition reused rather than new.

I'd close on **F-19.1** as the design target for this requirement, noting F-19.2 defers to R08. Agree, or do you want to carry F-19.2 explicitly?
Make it similar to the Initiate Takeover

Agreed — R19 mirrors R09 exactly, just inverted intent (relinquish instead of acquire).

**F-19.1 — Dispatch a control-handover request to a selected UAV.**

Same structural logic as F-09.1 (dispatch takeover request): pilot's goal is to signal intent to transfer the currently-managed UAV back to the UAV Pilot, initiating the handover negotiation (8.1.1). Response awareness (8.1.7) defers to the R08 notification stack, same as R09/R10 handled it.

**Closing Function: F-19.1 — Dispatch a control-handover request to a selected UAV.**

Moving to Behaviour.

Mirroring R09, one pathway per fixed modality plus mixed:

**Be-19.1.1 (Touch-only):** From the UAV's context — press-hold on the UAV glyph/map or open its detail panel → option ring surfaces a HANDOVER segment → tap to dispatch the request. Same press-hold option-ring pattern as R09/R14/R17.

**Be-19.1.2 (Keyboard-only):** Bezel OSS dedicated HANDOVER button (with UAV pre-selected via rotary/UCP), single press dispatches. Mirrors R09's dedicated-button/bezel path.

**Be-19.1.3 (Mixed):** UAV Detail/Status Panel (R12 chassis) exposes a HANDOVER row — reachable by touch tap or bezel OSS confirm — dispatches the request. Adds value as the third shared invocation surface, consistent with R09/R10's three-surface approach.

All three modality-complete: the request can be fully dispatched by Touch alone or Keyboard alone.

I'd carry all three (they're the same three shared surfaces as R09, reused). Agree, or collapse to one?
same logic as before, mirror the initiate takeover

Understood — R19 reuses R09's exact three shared invocation surfaces, inverted to HANDOVER.

**Closing Behaviour: Be-19.1.1 (Touch), Be-19.1.2 (Keyboard), Be-19.1.3 (Mixed)** — three shared invocation surfaces (option ring, dedicated bezel button, detail-panel row), modality-complete, mirroring R09.

Moving to Structure.

Same as R09/R10, reused not duplicated — only the HANDOVER label/action differs:

**S-19.1.1 (Dedicated control):** HANDOVER button — bezel OSS (Keyboard) + WAD touch affordance (Touch). Mirrors R09's dedicated takeover button, shared chassis.

**S-19.1.2 (Option-ring segment):** HANDOVER segment on the shared press-hold option ring anchored to the UAV glyph (Map/detail). Reuses R05/R09/R14/R17 ring pattern.

**S-19.1.3 (Detail-panel row):** HANDOVER row in the reused UAV Detail/Status Panel (R12 chassis), actionable via Touch tap or bezel OSS.

All three shared with R09's takeover surfaces — same widgets, added HANDOVER action. Response/ack (8.1.7) surfaces through the R08 notification stack, no new structure.

**Flag:** these are the identical surfaces as R09/R10/R17 — R19 adds only the HANDOVER action binding, not new hardware or new panels.

Close R19 on these three, or narrow to one?
same logic as before, mirror the initiate takeover

Confirmed — R19 closes as the full mirror of R09/R10, HANDOVER-inverted, all surfaces reused.

**R19 — CLOSED**

- **Function:** F-19.1 — Dispatch a control-handover request to a selected UAV.
- **Behaviour:** Be-19.1.1 (Touch), Be-19.1.2 (Keyboard), Be-19.1.3 (Mixed) — three shared invocation surfaces, modality-complete.
- **Structure:** S-19.1.1 (dedicated HANDOVER button, bezel OSS + WAD touch), S-19.1.2 (HANDOVER option-ring segment), S-19.1.3 (HANDOVER detail-panel row, R12 chassis). All reused from R09/R10/R17 with only the HANDOVER action binding added. Response/ack via R08 notification stack — no new structure.

**Summary:** R19 dispatches a UAV control-handover request through the same three shared invocation surfaces as the takeover (R09), adding only the HANDOVER action; no new hardware or panels.
